transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. When I try to talk things through with people, my thoughts get all jumbled and I can’t seem to keep a straight line in a conversation anymore. It has been making me quite worried, so my daughter helped me come in today.
Has this difficulty with your thoughts and memory happened suddenly over a few days or weeks, or has it been a gradual decline that you've noticed over several months or years?

It didn't happen all at once, doctor; it's been a very gradual change. These problems with my thoughts getting mixed up have been slowly creeping in for almost a year now, starting some time after my husband passed away.
Besides your difficulty with thoughts and memory, have you been experiencing a persistent feeling of sadness, hopelessness, or a loss of interest in the things you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or that I've lost interest in doing things. It's more that I want to join in, but I just get too jumbled and confused to participate like I used to. My mind gets so mixed up that it's hard to keep up with everyone.

Beyond these memory and thought difficulties, have you noticed any other changes, such as difficulty managing your finances, difficulty performing daily chores, or trouble finding your way around familiar places?

Yes, I've really struggled with those things. My daughter now has to come over every week to go through my mail, make sure my bills are paid on time, and keep track of my appointments. I also used to organize church dinners, but they have gently stopped including me in the planning, which makes me very sad.
Have you noticed any physical changes, such as stiffness in your movements, tremors, or significant difficulty with your balance and walking?
No, I haven't really noticed any stiffness, tremors, or problems with my balance. My walking is okay, it's really just my thoughts that feel so jumbled up.
Could you tell me how old you are currently?
I am 71 years old, doctor.

Have you noticed if your difficulty remembering recent events or learning new information seems to be the most prominent problem, or do you find that your primary struggle is with speaking and finding the right words?

It’s not really that I’m forgetting things or struggling to find words, doctor. My main problem is that my thoughts get completely jumbled, and I’ll start talking about the electric bill but then mix in my husband’s toolbox and the weather all at once. I just can't keep a straight line, and people get very confused trying to follow me.
When you have these jumbled thoughts, do you also experience significant periods of confusion that fluctuate throughout the day, where you might be much more clear-headed at some times than others?

I haven't really noticed my confusion fluctuating or having certain times of the day where I'm more clear-headed. It just seems like the jumbled thoughts happen whenever I try to have a conversation or focus on a task, no matter what time it is.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a condition like Parkinson's disease, or have you ever had a stroke or other significant vascular health issues like high blood pressure or diabetes?
No, doctor, I've never been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or had a stroke. As far as I know, I haven't had any major problems with high blood pressure or diabetes either.
When you have these difficulties, do you find it harder to perform complex tasks like managing your finances, or is it more of a struggle with your overall personality and memory for recent events?

Yes, I definitely struggle with complex tasks like managing my finances, and my daughter has to come over every week to handle my mail and bills so I don't miss payments. It isn't a problem with my personality or memory of recent events, but rather that my thoughts get too jumbled for me to keep those tasks straight.

When you think about your daily life, do you find that you struggle more with recognizing familiar faces or items, or is the difficulty primarily with keeping your focus and organizing your thoughts during tasks?

No, I don't have any trouble recognizing my daughter, my friends at church, or everyday things around the house. My struggle is definitely with keeping my focus and organizing my thoughts, which makes it so hard to manage my bills, plan choir songs, or even hold a simple conversation without getting all jumbled up.
